read.instructionDe: Lesen Sie die Karte. Tippen Sie auf ein Wort für seine Bedeutung.
read.instructionEn: Read the menu. Tap a word for its meaning.
read.text:
Café Bremen
Bei uns essen und trinken Sie gut!
Frühstück: Montag bis Samstag, 7 bis 11 Uhr
Frühstück mit Brot und Kaffee: 6 Euro
Suppe oder Salat: 5 Euro
Kuchen: 3 Euro
Tasse Kaffee oder Tee: 2 Euro
Glas Orangensaft: 3 Euro

questions.promptDe: Sie möchten Suppe und eine Tasse Tee. Was kostet das zusammen? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: You would like soup and a cup of tea. How much is that together? Choose the answer.
options: 5 euros.
7 euros.
8 euros.
questions.explanationDe: Auf der Karte steht: Suppe kostet 5 Euro, eine Tasse Tee kostet 2 Euro. Zusammen sind das 7 Euro.
questions.explanationEn: The menu says soup is 5 euros and a cup of tea is 2 euros. Together that is 7 euros.

questions.promptDe: Wann gibt es im Café Frühstück? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: When does the café serve breakfast? Choose the answer.
options: Monday to Saturday, from 7 to 11.
Monday to Friday, from 7 to 11.
Every day, from 7 to 11.
questions.explanationDe: Auf der Karte steht: Frühstück von Montag bis Samstag, 7 bis 11 Uhr. Am Sonntag ist kein Frühstück.
questions.explanationEn: The menu says breakfast is Monday to Saturday, 7 to 11. There is no breakfast on Sunday.

meaning.promptDe: Was möchte Ana? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What would Ana like? Choose the meaning.
options: She is hungry and orders a soup.
She is thirsty and orders a coffee.
She is tired and orders a tea.
meaning.answer: She is thirsty and orders a coffee.

meaning.promptDe: Hat Ana auch Hunger? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: Is Ana hungry too? Choose the meaning.
options: Yes, and she orders cake.
Yes, and she orders soup.
No, she only wants a drink.

meaning.promptDe: Was bestellt Ana noch? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
meaning.promptEn: What else does Ana order? Choose the answer.
options: A cup of tea and a mineral water.
A glass of orange juice and a beer.
A glass of mineral water and an orange juice.
meaning.answer: A glass of mineral water and an orange juice.

meaning.promptDe: Paul hat auch Tee, Bier und Wein. Was sagt Ana? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: Paul also has tea, beer and wine. What does Ana say? Choose the meaning.
options: Yes, please: she orders a glass of wine.
No, thank you: she will eat bread with salad.
No, thank you: she would like the bill.
meaning.answer: No, thank you: she will eat bread with salad.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt Paul? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does Paul say? Choose the meaning.
options: The waitress is coming right away with the bread.
The waitress is sorry: there is no bread today.
The bread will take another twenty minutes.
meaning.answer: The waitress is coming right away with the bread.

nextHook.de: Ana steht am Bahnhof und hat viele Fragen: Fährt der Zug nach Österreich? Und was kostet die Fahrkarte?
nextHook.en: Ana is at the station with a lot of questions: does the train go to Austria? And what does the ticket cost?

notes: Chunks are the five offer-and-answer pairs (Paul asks or offers, Ana answers); no boundary was in doubt. Each chunk has exactly one learner line, so the say lines (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) were not a choice. None of them is a dictation line (0, 4).

Read text: the café's menu with a price list and breakfast hours. Only Café and essen were missing from the dialogue; Café is the menu's heading and essen stands in the slogan „Bei uns essen und trinken Sie gut!“.
The café has no name anywhere in the course; I called it „Café Bremen“ (Bremen is on DIALOG_NAMES and is Ana's city). Rename it if the story has a name for it.
The prices are mine; the dialogue names none, so nothing can contradict them. The first read question makes the learner add two lines of the menu (5 + 2 euros).
Menu lines drop the article and „ein/eine“ („Tasse Kaffee oder Tee: 2 Euro“), as a printed menu does.

Existing data, dialogue line 7: „Ich esse ein Brot mit Salat.“ is glossed in English as „I’ll have a sandwich with salad.“ My meaning option says „bread with salad“ to stay with the German the learner hears; „ein Brot mit Salat“ is itself slightly odd German for what a café sells („ein belegtes Brot“ / „ein Sandwich“), though not wrong.

Existing data, dialogue line 9: Ana closes with „Zum Frühstück trinke ich immer eine Tasse Kaffee.“ after ordering in the afternoon-style scene; it reads as a line written to carry Frühstück and Tasse. It is the only learner line of the last chunk, so it is the say line.
Phonetik: MÖCH-te and HÖ-ren are word-stress items; SCHÖN is a one-syllable word and fails the item shape (needs at least two syllables), so the sound stage is pending for L9. Not changed.
